conflicts.subject: backend-app-sa
conflicts.explanation: Team 'security-team' granted a narrow permission (get on pods) via role 'pod-reader', but team 'backend-team' granted a wildcard permission via role 'backend-full-access' to the same subject 'backend-app-sa'. Since Kubernetes RBAC is purely additive, the wildcard grant makes the narrow restriction meaningless.

Team 'security-team' created the policy 'allowed-image-repos' (allowed image repos: ['mycompany.com/']), but it only applies to ['team-security']. The namespace(s) ['team-backend', 'team-data'] have no equivalent protection, even though they run similar workloads. Deployments in ['team-backend', 'team-data'] can silently bypass this security control.

Team 'backend-team' granted RBAC access (role 'trigger-data-jobs') for 'team-backend/backend-app-sa' to act in namespace 'team-data'. However, team 'data-team' has a default-deny NetworkPolicy ('default-deny-ingress') in that same namespace. RBAC authorization will succeed, but any actual network traffic will be silently dropped at the network layer — a misalignment between the control plane and data plane that neither team can see from their own policy alone.
